questions.question: If one angle of triangle PQR is greater than the sum of the other two, the triangle PQR will be:
questions.questionHtml: If one angle of triangle PQR is greater than the sum of the other two, the triangle PQR will be:
questions.solution:
Given:

If one angle of triangle PQR is greater than the sum of the other two, the triangle PQR will be?

Formula Used:

In a triangle, if one angle is greater than the sum of the other two angles, then that triangle is an obtuse triangle.

Calculation:

Let the angles of triangle PQR be A, B, and C.

Given that A > B + C

Since the sum of the angles in any triangle is 180°:

A + B + C = 180°

From the given condition:

A > B + C

⇒ A > 90° (since B + C < 90°)

⇒ Triangle PQR is an obtuse triangle.

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: The perimeters of two similar ΔABC and Δ PQR are 48.4 cm and 12.1 cm, respectively. What is the ratio of the areas of Δ ABC and Δ PQR?
questions.questionHtml: The perimeters of two similar ΔABC and ΔPQR are 48.4 cm and 12.1 cm, respectively. What is the ratio of the areas of ΔABC and ΔPQR?
questions.solution:
Given:

The perimeters of two similar ΔABC and ΔPQR are 48.4 cm and 12.1 cm

Concept used:

Area ΔABC/ Area ΔPQR = (Perimeter of ΔABC/Perimeter of ΔPQR)2

Calculation:

Area ΔABC/ Area ΔPQR = [(48.4)/(12.1)]2

⇒ Area ΔABC/ Area ΔPQR = (4/1)2

⇒ Area ΔABC/ Area ΔPQR = 16/1

∴ The required ratio is 16 : 1.

questions.question: In an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle is four times the sum of the base angles. The measure of the square root of the vertex angle is:
questions.questionHtml: In an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle is four times the sum of the base angles. The measure of the square root of the vertex angle is:
questions.solution:
Given:

In an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle is four times the sum of the base angles.

Formula used:

Let the base angle be x.

Vertex angle = 4(2x) (since the sum of base angles is 2x)

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180º

Calculation:

2x + 4(2x) = 180º

⇒ 2x + 8x = 180º

⇒ 10x = 180º

⇒ x = 18º

Vertex angle = 4(2x) = 4(36º) = 144º

Square root of the vertex angle = √144º = 12º

∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questions.question: A triangle with the lengths of its sides proportional to the numbers 7, 24 and 30 is:
questions.questionHtml: A triangle with the lengths of its sides proportional to the numbers 7, 24 and 30 is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For any triangle with sides a, b, and c (where c is the longest side), the type of triangle is determined by comparing a2 + b2 and c2.

Here, the sides are proportional to 7, 24, and 30. Let a = 7, b = 24, and c = 30.

Calculate: 72 + 242 = 49 + 576 = 625.

Calculate: 302 = 900.

Since 900 > 625 (i.e., c2 > a2 + b2), the triangle is obtuse angled.

∴ The correct answer is obtuse angled.

Alternate Method

Given: The ratios of the lengths of the sides of a triangle are 7 : 24 : 30.

Formula Used:

1. Triangle Inequality: Sum of any two sides must be greater than the third side (a + c).

2. Cosine Property:

• If a2 + b2 > c2 → Acute-angled triangle.

• If a2 + b2 = c2 → Right-angled triangle.

• If a2 + b2 < c2 → Obtuse-angled triangle.

Calculations:

⇒ Let the sides be a = 7k, b = 24k, and c = 30k.

⇒ First, check triangle validity: 7k + 24k = 31k. Since 31k > 30k, the triangle is possible.

⇒ Now, compare the squares of the sides: a2 = (7k)2 = 49k2.

⇒ b2 = (24k)2 = 576k2.

⇒ c2 = (30k)2 = 900k2.

⇒ Sum of squares of smaller sides = 49k2 + 576k2 = 625k2.

⇒ Comparing a2 + b2 and c2: 625k2 < 900k2.

⇒ Since a2 + b2 < c2, the angle opposite to side c is obtuse (greater than 90°).

∴ The correct answer is obtuse angled.

Additional Information

Triangle Inequality Theorem

The sum of the lengths of any two sides of a triangle must be strictly greater than the length of the third side (a + c).

Pythagorean Triplets

If a2 + b2 = c2, the triangle is right-angled. Common examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (7, 24, 25).

Cosine Rule and Angles

For triangle ABC, cos C = (a2 + b2 − c2) ÷ (2ab). If the numerator is negative (a2 + b2 < c2), angle C is obtuse.

questions.question: In triangle DEF, the bisector of angle D intersects side EF at point N. If DE = 36 cm, DF = 40 cm and EF = 38 cm, then the length (in cm) of NF is _____.

questions.solution:
By the Angle Bisector Theorem:

EN / NF = DE / DF

EN / NF = 36 / 40

EN = 9x

NF = 10x

EN + NF = 38

⇒ 9x + 10x = 38

⇒ x = 2

NF = 10x = 10 × 2 = 20

questions.question: The radius of the incircle of an equilateral triangle is 9√3 cm. What will be the perimeter of this equilateral triangle?
questions.questionHtml: The radius of the incircle of an equilateral triangle is 9√3 cm. What will be the perimeter of this equilateral triangle?
questions.solution:
Given:

The radius of the incircle of an equilateral triangle = 9√3 cm

Concept Used:

In an equilateral triangle, the radius of the incircle is related to the side length (s) by the formula:

The radius of incircle = side / 2√3

Calculation:

Radius of incircle = side / 2√3

⇒ 9√3 = side / 2√3

⇒ side = 9√3 × 2√3 = 18 × 3 = 54 cm

So, Perimeter of an equilateral triangle = 3 × side = 3 × 54 = 162 cm

∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questions.question: In a right-angled triangle PQR, ∠Q = 90°. A and B are the mid-points of PQ and PR, respectively. If PQ = 16 cm, QR = 30 cm and PR = 34 cm, what is perimeter (in cm) of the trapezium ABRQ?
questions.questionHtml: In a right-angled triangle PQR, ∠Q = 90°. A and B are the mid-points of PQ and PR, respectively. If PQ = 16 cm, QR = 30 cm and PR = 34 cm, what is perimeter (in cm) of the trapezium ABRQ?
questions.solution:
Given:

In a right-angled triangle PQR, ∠Q = 90°.

A and B are the mid-points of PQ and PR, respectively.

PQ = 16 cm, QR = 30 cm and PR = 34 cm, 

Concept used:

Pythagoras Theorem

Calculation:

    

Considering ΔPQR,

PQ2 + QR2 = PR2

⇒ 162 + 302 = PR2

⇒ PR = \(√ {16^2 + 30^2}\)

⇒ PR = \(√ {1156}\)

⇒ PR = 34

According to the question,

PA = AQ = 16/2 = 8 cm

PB = BR = 34/2 = 17 cm

Now, ΔPAB is a right-angled triangle at A.

Considering ΔPAB,

PA2 + AB2 = PB2

⇒ 82 + AB2 = 172

⇒ AB2 = 289 - 64

⇒ AB = √225

⇒ AB = 15

Now, the perimeter of the trapezium ABRQ = 15 + 17 + 30 + 8 = 70 cm

∴ The perimeter of the trapezium ABRQ is 70 cm.

Therefore, third side = 6 cm.

questions.question: In the given triangle, CD is the bisector of ∠BCA. CD = DA. If ∠BDC = 76°, What is the degree measure of ∠CBD?
questions.questionHtml: In the given triangle, CD is the bisector of ∠BCA. CD = DA. If ∠BDC = 76°, What is the degree measure of ∠CBD?
questions.solution:
CD is the bisector of ∠BCA.

⇒ ∠BCD = ∠DCA = θ, CD = DA               [Given]

⇒ ∠DCA = ∠CAD = θ  ⇒ ∠BDC = 76°                    [Given]

⇒ ∠BDC = ∠DCA + ∠CAD ⇒ θ + θ = 76°  ⇒ 2θ = 76° ⇒ θ = 38° 

In triangle CBD,

∠BCD + ∠CDB + ∠CBD = 180° ⇒ θ  + 76° + ∠CBD = 180° 

⇒ 38°  + 76° + ∠CBD = 180° ⇒ ∠CBD = 180° - 114° ⇒ ∠CBD = 66°

questions.questionHtml: In triangle ABC, AB = AC and ∠A = 70º. Find the value of ∠C.
questions.solution:
Given:

In triangle ABC, AB = AC and ∠A = 70º.

Formula Used:

In an isosceles triangle, the base angles are equal.

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180º

Calculation:

Let ∠B = ∠C = x

∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180º

⇒ 70º + x + x = 180º

⇒ 70º + 2x = 180º

⇒ 2x = 180º - 70º

⇒ 2x = 110º

⇒ x = 55º

∴ The correct answer is option (4).

questions.question: In an isosceles triangle ABC, AB=AC. D is a point inside the triangle such that ∠BAD = 20° = ∠DCB, ∠CAD = 80°. The value of ∠ABC is:
questions.questionHtml: In an isosceles triangle ABC, AB=AC. D is a point inside the triangle such that ∠BAD = 20° = ∠DCB, ∠CAD = 80°. The value of ∠ABC is:
questions.solution:
Given:

In an isosceles triangle ABC, AB = AC.

∠BAD = 20°

∠DCB = 20°

∠CAD = 80°

Formula Used:

In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite the equal sides are equal.

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°

Calculation:

Since AB = AC, ∠ABC = ∠ACB.

In triangle ABD:

∠BAD + ∠ADB + ∠ABD = 180°

∠BAD = 20°

∠CAD = 80°, so ∠BAC = 100° (since ∠BAD + ∠CAD = ∠BAC)

In triangle ABC:

Since AB = AC, ∠ABC = ∠ACB

The sum of the angles in triangle ABC:

∠BAC + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180°

Substitute ∠BAC = 100° and ∠ABC = ∠ACB:

100° + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180°

∠ABC + ∠ACB = 80°

Since ∠ABC = ∠ACB:

2 × ∠ABC = 80°

∠ABC = 40°

The value of ∠ABC is 40°

questions.question: In ΔABC, P and Q are the middle points of the sides AB and AC, respectively. R is a point on the segment PQ such that PR : RQ = 1 : 4. If PR = 5 cm, then BC = ?
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, P and Q are the middle points of the sides AB and AC, respectively. R is a point on the segment PQ such that PR : RQ = 1 : 4. If PR = 5 cm, then BC = ?
questions.solution:
PR : RQ = 1 : 4 ⇒ PQ (1 + 4) = 5 units = 5 × 5 = 25 cm

So the measure of line BC = 2 × 25 = 50 cm

questions.question: In right-angled triangle ABC, ∠C=90, CM is perpendicular on AB. If AB = 18 cm and BM = 6 cm, then find the length of CM.
questions.questionHtml: In right-angled triangle ABC, ∠C=90, CM is perpendicular on AB. If AB = 18 cm and BM = 6 cm, then find the length of CM.
questions.solution:
AB = 18 cm, BM = 6 cm, AM = 18 - 6 = 12 cm.

 

Using Pythagoras theorem in ΔABC: a2 + b2 = c2

 

Area of ΔABC = Area of ΔAMC + Area of ΔCMB

 

(1/2) × 18 × h = (1/2) × 12 × h + (1/2) × 6 × h

 

9h = 6h + 3h , 9h = 9h , h = 6√2

questions.question: In ΔABC, DE || BC in such a way that A-D-B and A-E-C are equal. If ∠ACB = 40°, then ∠DAE + ∠ADE = ____.
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, DE || BC in such a way that A-D-B and A-E-C are equal. If  ∠ACB = 40°, then  ∠DAE +  ∠ADE = ____.
questions.solution:
We have a triangle ABC in which DE // BC 

So, the \(\angle\)ACB = \(\angle\)AED = \(40^\circ\) (corresponding angles as DE//BC and AC is a transversal line which intersects them) 

Now,  consider the  triangle ADE as we know that 

Sum of the  angles of a triangle = 180 

⇒ \(\angle\)ADE +\(\angle\) DAE + \(\angle\)AED = 180  ⇒ \(\angle\)ADE + \(\angle\)DAE + 40 = 180

⇒ \(\angle\)ADE + \(\angle\)DAE = \(140^\circ\)

questions.question: The centroid of an equilateral triangle PQR is L. If PQ = 6 cm, the length of PL is:
questions.questionHtml: The centroid of an equilateral triangle PQR is L. If PQ = 6 cm, the length of PL is:
questions.solution:
Circumradius of Equilateral triangle = side of equilateral triangle/√3

PL = PQ/√3 ⇒ PL = 6/√3 ⇒ PL = 2√3 cm.

questions.question: P, Q and R are the three angles of a triangle. If P - Q = 20 ∘ and Q - R = 26 ∘ , then ∠P is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: P, Q and R are the three angles of a triangle. If P - Q = 20<sup>∘</sup>  and Q - R = 26<sup>∘</sup> , then ∠P is equal to:
questions.solution:
P - Q = 20°, Q - R = 26° ⇒ P = Q + 20°, Q = R + 26°

P + Q + R = 180 ⇒ (R + 46) + (R + 26) + R = 180

3R + 72 = 180 ⇒ 3R = 108 ⇒ R = 36

Q = 36 + 26 = 62

P = 62 + 20 = 82

questions.question: What is the area of a quadrilateral ABCD, (shown below) in which sides AB and BC are equal, sides AD and CD are of lengths 5 cm and 13 cm. respectively, and side AD is perpendicular to the diagonal AC?
questions.questionHtml: What is the area of a quadrilateral ABCD, (shown below) in which sides AB and BC are equal, sides AD and CD are of lengths 5 cm and 13 cm. respectively, and side AD is perpendicular to the diagonal AC?

options.html: 75 cm2
80 cm2
78 cm2
82 cm2

questions.solution:
Given:

AB = BC = 10 cm

AD = 5 cm, CD = 13 cm

Calculation:

In Δ ADC

AC = √{CD2 - AD2} = √{132 - 52} = √144 = 12 cm

So,

Area of Δ ADC = 1/2 × AD × AC = 1/2 × 5 × 12 = 30 cm2

Now,

In Δ ABC

AB = BC = 10 cm and AC = 12 cm

∵ In an isosceles triangle, altitude is equal to the perpendicular bisector

So, AE = EC = 1/2 × 12 = 6 cm 

BE = √{102 - 62} = √{100 - 36} = √64 = 8 cm

So,

Area of triangle ABC = 1/2 × AC × BE = 1/2 × 12 × 8 = 48 cm²

Thus, Total Area = 48 + 30 = 78 cm²

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: In ΔPQR, M, N, and S are the mid-points of sides PQ, PR, and QR, respectively. If the area of ΔPQR is 46 cm², what is the area (in cm²) of the quadrilateral MNRQ?
questions.questionHtml: In ΔPQR, M, N, and S are the mid-points of sides PQ, PR, and QR, respectively. If the area of ΔPQR is 46 cm², what is the area (in cm²) of the quadrilateral MNRQ?

Area of ΔPQR = 46 cm2

Area of each smaller triangle = 46 / 4 = 11.5 cm2

Area of quadrilateral MNRQ = 3 × 11.5 = 34.5 cm2
